introduction: On this Sunday, Isaiah says that God's word is like rain that waters the earth and does not return without bearing fruit. In the Gospel, Jesus tells the parable of the sower, whose seed falls on the path, on rocky ground, among thorns and on good soil. Paul says that all creation groans as it waits for the glory of God's children. Let us receive the word of God like good soil.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, God's word does not return to him empty. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may sow the word of God generously in every place. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those whose hearts are hardened or distracted: that the word of God may find room to grow in them. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those whose faith is shallow and easily discouraged: that they may put down deep roots. Let us pray to the Lord.
For creation, which groans and waits for redemption: that we may care for the earth God has given us. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may hear the word, understand it and bear fruit. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, your word is like rain that makes the earth fruitful. Make our hearts good soil, so that your word may bear fruit in us a hundredfold. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Good soil
reflection.body:
Isaiah compares God's word to the rain and snow, which water the earth and make it fruitful before returning to the sky. "so is my word that goes out of my mouth: it will not return to me void, but it will accomplish that which I please." God's word always does its work.

In the Gospel, Jesus sits in a boat and teaches the crowd on the shore with a parable. A sower goes out and scatters seed. Some falls on the path and is eaten by birds. Some falls on rocky ground, springs up quickly, and withers in the sun. Some falls among thorns and is choked. And some falls on good soil and produces "some one hundred times as much, some sixty, and some thirty."

The sower is generous, even wasteful, scattering seed everywhere. That is how God sows his word: to everyone, everywhere.

Jesus explains the parable to his disciples. The path is the person who hears the word without understanding, and "the evil one comes and snatches away" what was sown. The rocky ground is the one who receives the word with joy but "has no root," and falls away when trouble comes. The thorny ground is the one in whom "the cares of this age and the deceitfulness of riches choke the word." The good soil is the one "who hears the word and understands it, who most certainly bears fruit."

Most of us are a mixture of all four soils. The question is not only what kind of soil we are, but how we can prepare our hearts to become good soil.

Paul looks at the whole of creation "groaning" and waiting for its redemption, as a field waits for harvest. This week, look at your own heart. What snatches the word away, what keeps it from taking root, what chokes it? Spend time each day with a passage of Scripture, and let it grow.
